headline: GOLD JUMPS to $4,750/oz as US-Iran peace deal hopes reignite precious metals rally
snippet: Spot gold jumped to $4,750/oz and silver surged 3% to $79.62 as markets priced in the possibility of a US-Iran ceasefire ending the 69-day conflict; market watchers told CNBC the secular bull market — which saw gold rise 66% and silver 135% in 2025 — may have found its next leg higher.

headline: SSR MINING SURGES 20% on blowout Q1: $4,770/oz avg gold, $1.5B Copler mine sale
snippet: SSR Mining posted a blowout Q1 with EPS of $1.15 — nearly three times year-over-year — on 84% revenue growth, driven by an average realized gold price of $4,770/oz; the company also announced a $1.5B sale of its suspended 80% Copler stake in Turkey, sharply derisking the portfolio.

headline: LION ZONE BEST EVER: Power Metallic hits 22m @ 11.46% CuEq at Nisk, Quebec
snippet: Power Metallic Mines drilled 22.00m grading 11.46% copper equivalent — including 6.5m at 18.59% CuEq — at the Lion Zone of its Nisk polymetallic project in Quebec, the company's second-best intersection ever, as it advances toward a maiden resource estimate targeted for Q3 2026.

headline: G2 GOLDFIELDS drills 84.5m @ 3.0 g/t Au from 915m, extends OKO to 1km depth
snippet: G2 Goldfields extended its high-grade OKO gold deposit in Guyana to 1 kilometre of vertical depth with an 84.5m intercept grading 3.0 g/t gold from 915m — the company's deepest-ever hole, with mineralization remaining open and the system potentially far larger than current resources suggest.

headline: G7 TO CHINA: weaponizing critical minerals supply chains 'will fail'
snippet: G7 trade ministers meeting in Paris committed to ensuring China cannot 'weaponise economic dependencies in mineral supply chains' and condemned rare earth export restrictions as economic coercion — though significant US-EU divides over implementation prevented any binding timelines from being agreed.

headline: CHINA CUTS sulfuric acid exports — a fifth of global copper supply now at risk
snippet: China halted sulfuric acid exports effective May 1, threatening heap-leach operations that supply roughly a fifth of global copper production; Chile — which imports over 1 million tonnes of Chinese acid annually — faces a structural deficit as spot acid prices have doubled since February and second-half supply remains largely uncovered.

headline: 100+ NEW US LITHIUM PROJECTS proposed as energy storage demand surges 55%
snippet: More than 100 new lithium extraction sites have been proposed across the United States as soaring demand for EV batteries and grid energy storage — up 55% year-over-year — drives a domestic mining boom, though permitting timelines and community opposition remain significant hurdles to bringing capacity online.

headline: HECLA probes Greens Creek tailings recovery to wring more from North America's top silver mine
snippet: Hecla Mining is investigating a tailings recovery project at Greens Creek — North America's largest silver-producing mine — aimed at extracting substantially more value from the southeast Alaska operation while reducing long-term environmental management and reclamation costs.

headline: Standard Uranium locks in DAVIDSON RIVER drill targets — two rigs mobilize May 31
snippet: Standard Uranium has finalized drill targets at its Davidson River project in Saskatchewan's southwest Athabasca Basin following ExoSphere multiphysics surveys, with two rigs mobilizing May 31 to test the Warrior, Bronco, and Thunderbird conductor corridors — its first drilling at the property since 2022.

headline: Can USA Rare Earth's $2.8B SERRA VERDE deal break China's 85% refining grip?
snippet: The Diplomat examines whether USA Rare Earth's $2.8B acquisition of Brazil's Serra Verde mine can meaningfully challenge China's 70% share of global rare earth mine output and 85% control of refining capacity, given that building processing infrastructure takes 3-7 years and Chinese price manipulation remains a structural threat to new entrants.

headline: AFRICA winning the junior mining exploration race in 2026 — who's ahead and why
snippet: A new analysis finds African junior miners are outpacing global peers in the 2026 exploration race, driven by underexplored geology, competitive royalty structures, and growing demand from major miners for bolt-on acquisitions — though security risk and permitting uncertainty in some jurisdictions remain key variables.
